title: Define module interfaces and required outputs for VPC Terraform modules (alpha)
creator: Irene Choi
description:
Goal
Lock the public inputs/outputs for the AWS Private VPC Terraform module suite for alpha so Solutions Eng + customers can adopt without churn, and so the Redwood Private installer has stable expectations.

Scope
- Define minimal required inputs and stable outputs for:
  - module.vpc (VPC + subnets + routing + NAT)
  - module.endpoints (Interface/Gateway endpoints + Private DNS behavior)
  - module.logging (VPC flow logs destinations + retention hooks)
  - module.security_groups (opinionated SG patterns for EKS/private deployment)
  - module.iam_installer (execution role scaffold + permission boundary pattern)
  - module.connectivity_hooks (VPN/DX placeholders: outputs + route table hooks only)
- Align with Private installer preflight checks (endpoints + DNS) and doc expectations.
- Mark which interface elements are ALPHA-locked (no breaking changes without version bump + release note).

Non-goals
- Encoding enterprise-specific topologies (Transit Gateway, custom DNS resolvers, third-party firewalls) beyond supported extension points.
- Providing a fully turnkey EKS cluster module.

Proposed alpha contract (draft)
1) module.vpc
Required inputs:
- name (string): environment name prefix
- region (string)
- vpc_cidr (string)
- az_count (number, default 3)
Optional inputs (alpha-supported):
- public_subnet_cidrs (list) OR derived
- private_subnet_cidrs (list) OR derived
- enable_ipv6 (bool, default false)
- nat_strategy (string: per_az | single | none; default per_az)
- tags (map)
Stable outputs:
- vpc_id
- vpc_cidr
- public_subnet_ids
- private_subnet_ids
- private_route_table_ids
- public_route_table_ids
- nat_gateway_ids (may be empty)
- availability_zones
Notes:
- For Redwood Private alpha we assume workloads live in private subnets; public subnets exist only for NAT/LB depending on customer ingress pattern.

2) module.endpoints
Required inputs:
- vpc_id
- private_subnet_ids
- security_group_ids (endpoint SG)
- enable_private_dns (bool; default true)
Optional inputs:
- enabled_endpoints (list; default set below)
- additional_interface_endpoints (list)
- route_table_ids_for_gateway_endpoints (list)
Default endpoints (alpha):
- Gateway: s3
- Interface: ecr.api, ecr.dkr, sts, logs, monitoring, ec2, autoscaling, elasticloadbalancing (EKS common), kms (recommended)
Stable outputs:
- interface_endpoint_ids
- interface_endpoint_dns_entries (serialized list string for now; see note)
- gateway_endpoint_ids
- endpoints_enabled
Installer expectation mapping:
- ECR pulls require ecr.api + ecr.dkr with Private DNS enabled OR documented alternative.

3) module.logging
Required inputs:
- vpc_id
Optional inputs:
- flow_logs_destination (cloudwatch | s3 | none; default cloudwatch)
- cloudwatch_log_group_name (optional; default derived)
- retention_days (default 30)
- s3_bucket_arn (if destination=s3)
Stable outputs:
- flow_logs_status (enabled/disabled)
- flow_logs_destination
- flow_logs_log_group_arn (if cloudwatch)
- flow_logs_s3_bucket_arn (if s3)

4) module.security_groups
Required inputs:
- vpc_id
Optional inputs:
- allowed_egress_cidrs (default 0.0.0.0/0 but discouraged; see secure mode)
- allow_https_egress (bool default true)
- allow_dns_to_vpc_resolver (bool default true)
Stable outputs:
- sg_endpoints_id
- sg_cluster_nodes_id
- sg_internal_lb_id
- sg_egress_id

5) module.iam_installer
Required inputs:
- name
Optional inputs:
- permission_boundary_arn (recommended)
- trusted_principals (list)
Stable outputs:
- installer_role_arn
- installer_role_name
- installer_policy_arn

6) module.connectivity_hooks
Required inputs:
- vpc_id
- private_route_table_ids
Optional inputs:
- vpn_route_cidrs (list)
Stable outputs:
- route_table_ids
- suggested_propagation_targets (document only)

Open questions to close in review
- Do we output endpoint DNS entries as structured list (preferred) vs a serialized string to keep module interface stable across TF versions?
- NAT strategy defaults: per_az vs single for cost-sensitive pilots (Infra leaning per_az for availability; SE asking for single-nat example).
- Which endpoints are strictly required vs recommended for alpha (installer preflight needs clarity).

Acceptance criteria
- Confluence/README section enumerating inputs/outputs per module, with “alpha locked” callouts.
- Private installer team sign-off: required outputs present and names match what preflight will query.
- Security sign-off: defaults + extension points are safe-by-default (no accidental public egress due to missing endpoints).
- Follow-up issues created for any remaining open questions; no lingering ambiguity in alpha docs.

Links
- PRs implementing current interfaces:
  - redwood-terraform#18422 (core vpc)
  - redwood-terraform#18437 (endpoints + DNS)
  - redwood-terraform#18455 (flow logs)
  - redwood-terraform#18474 (security groups)
  - redwood-terraform#18491 (iam scaffold)
- Installer preflight alignment:
  - redwood-private-installer#19110
comments: 2025-06-06 (Victor Alvarez): Drafted initial interface table for vpc/endpoints/logging modules. Biggest risk is endpoint DNS outputs — Terraform provider returns nested objects; proposing we output both raw IDs and a flattened list of DNS names. Need to decide what we treat as stable for alpha.

2025-06-07 (Nina Petrova): For EKS private control plane cases, make sure private_subnet_ids are the ones with required tags and that we don’t accidentally encourage placing worker nodes in public subnets. Output naming should avoid ambiguity (private_subnet_ids vs node_subnet_ids). Suggest we standardize on private_subnet_ids for everything and let the EKS module/installer interpret.

2025-06-10 (Marcus Lin): Security note: defaults should not assume 0.0.0.0/0 egress if endpoints are enabled. Recommend we document a “restricted egress” mode: only allow HTTPS to AWS endpoints via interface endpoints + S3 gateway endpoint, and explicit opt-in for internet egress. Even if we don’t enforce via NACLs, SG patterns should guide the safe default.

2025-06-11 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE perspective, outputs must include flow logs destination + log group ARN so we can verify logging at install time and wire to runbooks. Also please include vpc_cidr and AZ list in outputs so troubleshooting doesn’t rely on state access.

2025-06-13 (Bruno Silva): Implemented flattening helper in endpoints module to output `interface_endpoint_dns_entries` as a newline-delimited string to avoid TF type drift across versions. I’m not thrilled with this, but it’s stable. If we want a list output, we should pin provider behavior and add integration test assertions.

2025-06-17 (Irene Choi): Please avoid string-encoding collections unless we absolutely must. Alpha is already hard; we’ll regret parsing later. If provider pinning is the lever, let’s do that. Action: Victor + Sahana to propose a stable list-of-strings output and add integration test coverage in ENG-4860.

2025-06-20 (Simran Kaur): Reference architecture calls out required endpoints for image pulls (ECR) and logs (CloudWatch Logs). The module interface doc should explicitly label endpoints as REQUIRED vs RECOMMENDED and align with installer preflight messaging so customers don’t get surprised mid-install.

2025-06-24 (Kevin Osei): For flow logs to CloudWatch, ensure the module either creates the log group with retention and KMS option or clearly documents the expected existing resources. Output should include whether encryption is enabled (even if just ‘kms_key_id’ output or ‘none’).

2025-07-02 (Victor Alvarez): Updated draft interface contract: endpoints output is now list(string) for DNS names; provider pinned in repo (see CI PR). Added required vs recommended endpoint list. Waiting on Private installer team to confirm naming matches preflight checks.

2025-07-08 (Colin O'Donnell): Field feedback: customers want to know exactly which outputs to hand to the installer. Suggest we add a short ‘handoff block’ in docs showing a terraform output -> installer config mapping (vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, endpoint_private_dns_enabled, log_group_arn).
